title: How Buddy Petit played, his California trip and his habits
summary: Foster describes Buddy Petit's own style, sweet or hot, his trip to California with George Washington where he got sick, and how he lived as a bachelor.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: It's possible that Rickard may have told us. We interviewed him a few years ago. Yeah, he put it out on him. That's right. Maybe we already have it on tape, so don't worry about it at present. You probably might have it already. Yeah, we may have it. We did interview Rickard. We talked about his family as much as we could remember to ask him about it. I was going to ask some more about Buddy Petit. How did he play? Was he really good? Some people say he was very good. I was just wondering if he was one of the best, or what did you say?
He was one of the best, or what did you say? He had his own style. He had his own style. He didn't. But he had his own style.
Is he extra loud, or fast, or high, or low, or any special things about the way he played?

Well, I'll tell you about Buddy. Buddy, for you some of all kind of choppy. For you the beautifulest. I see you down on, what's this one? Is that an example? That goes to Richland? Yeah. Is that a example? Yeah. If I ever go to Richland. No, that's LaFouche. If I ever go down on LaFouche, yeah, Buddy LaFouche is there. I see you down on Buddy LaFouche, and those people were playing with the white dancers, and his brothers playing, during this time, his voice came out, my buddy. You know, they used to preach to him on that. And that man could play the sweeter music, you know, on that trumpet. It's soft and sweet. It's the best he could play loud, or the hot. You know, the hot. He was that. He's just not the all-around trumpet man. And during that time, when he came over there, I think he and George had made that trip to California. You don't know anything about that. No, no, no, no. They had made that trip to California. Then the first one was that he did. That's right. What year was that? Well, I couldn't exactly, it was a year. I didn't know him at the time.
He told me, you know. You didn't know him at that time? No, he had went to, he and George Washington, the family, went to California.
Oh, no, George used to travel a whole lot.
Yeah, George used to travel a whole lot.
Did he say anything about his trip to California? Were they enjoying it?
Yeah, he said he had a wonderful trip out there. And the only way he came home, because he had got Mexican fever.
He had got Mexican fever. Mexican fever? That's right, and that's why he came home. Got sick out there. He used to talk to me all the time. Same thing with you.
There's a piano player out there, Jelly Roll Martin, that says he went out and joined his band out there. Maybe that's the date that he played then.
Buddy? Yeah, Buddy. Well, there was only two of them out there. He and George.

So he joined some other band out there, I guess. He did, he did. I think, though, this article I read about this pianist talked like Frankie Dooson went out there with him, wasn't it? Do you remember? There was a story about Frankie Dooson. There was one story. Yeah, Frankie Dooson went too, but he was a trombonist. Do you remember? Yeah.

Now I played with him too. Now sometime, I was able to play him. Oh, really? And I was playing with them people. You didn't think about it. That's right. I know he said it is that, but he was a rapper on Ballon Street, or a cemetery. I went to his house several times, and I called myself, I was a boy, you know. He used to come up, you know, he was a kind of bachelor, you know. Sometimes he'd go up there and fry eggs, you know. Yeah. Cooked living or the same thing he'd do. He used to play a job. He wasn't a regular family man, but he used to play, you know, play a job with him.
